project_overview.name: Course Translation Hub
project_overview.description: An unzipped IMSCC Canvas course export used as a hub for translating course content.

core_files.imsmanifest.xml: The main manifest file. It maps resource identifiers (used in the hash directories) to their corresponding files and outlines the course structure (modules, item sequences). Treat this as the definitive index.
core_files.app/link_mapping.json: A multi-language JSON mapping of English web links to their localized counterparts (PTBR, SPA, etc.). Used by the LinkProcessor (in app/core/) to automatically replace links before bot translation. Lives inside the app/ directory alongside the controller.

directories.course_settings/: Contains global configuration files for the course, including the main syllabus page (e.g., syllabus.html) and course_settings.xml (which provides the course code).
directories.wiki_content/: Contains Canvas Pages stored as standard HTML files. These are primary targets for textual translation.
directories.web_resources/: Contains static files, images, or documents linked within the course pages.
directories.non_cc_assessments/: Contains quizzes and assessments that might not follow the standard Common Cartridge specification.
directories.hash_directories/: Folders named with unique alphanumeric hashes (e.g., 'g038b...'). These contain metadata for assignments, discussions, quizzes, and rubrics (e.g., assessment_meta.xml, assessment_qti.xml, assignment_settings.xml). Look inside these XML files for description tags and text that require translation.
directories.app/: Contains the main application code: controller.py, main_ui.py, course_auditor.py, reprocess_failed.py, and the architecture instructions JSON.
directories.app/bots/: Contains the specialized translation and auditing bots (html_bot.py, xml_bot.py, txt_bot.py, image_bot.py, auditor_bot.py, scripturecheck_bot.py, qa_audit_bot.py, api_utils.py), plus the shared translation_log.txt.
directories.app/core/: Contains the modularized architecture components: LinkProcessor (link_processor.py), WorkspaceManager (workspace_manager.py), and DashboardGenerator (dashboard_generator.py), decoupled from the main controller.
directories.Glossary/: Contains a unified 'glossary.json' for terms standardization and a 'scriptures/' subfolder containing language-specific subfolders (por/, spa/) with modern scriptures used to crosscheck references.
directories.Courses to Translate/: Contains the temporary course files, including the raw .imscc Canvas exports and their respective unzipped working directories. Finalized translations (e.g., _PTBR output folders) and repackaged .imscc files are also saved here.
directories.Courses to Audit/: Contains the .imscc Canvas exports (English Canon and Translated versions) to be unzipped and compared by the course auditor process.
directories.Reports/: Contains all generated output reports. Both the translation dashboard Excel ('{CourseName} Translation Report.xlsx') and the audit report Excel ('Audit_Report_{CourseName}.xlsx') are saved here.

bot_instructions.workspace_management: All controllers and scripts must strictly look for and operate on unzipped course exports and raw .imscc files exclusively within the 'Courses to Translate/' directory. Finalized translations (e.g., _PTBR output folders) and repackaged .imscc files must also be saved directly into the 'Courses to Translate/' directory. The root hub directory must remain clean of course files.
bot_instructions.temporary_override: CRITICAL: The user currently only has the Gemini API key. All agents (including HTML, XML, QTI, Document, and Image bots) MUST temporarily use Gemini instead of Claude or ChatGPT.
bot_instructions.mandatory_pre_check: All agent bots MUST read this file (Course_Translation_Hub_ArchitectureAndInstructions.json) before beginning any translation tasks.
logging_requirements: All bots (including the controller and specialized bots) MUST implement an internal logging mechanism.
All bots and the controller must append their logs to a single shared text-based log file (translation_log.txt) in the app/bots/ directory. Individual log files are not used.
Every significant action, such as file delegation, successful translation, skipped files, errors, and warnings, must be recorded in the shared log file as well as printed to standard output.
The controller bot must extract the Course Name and Course Code from the imsmanifest.xml or course_settings.xml and log it as '[System] CourseInfo: {course_name}|{course_code}'.

The controller bot must log link mapping actions (e.g., GoogleLinkStripped, SkippedLink, SkippedLinkWithComment, CommentedLink) to track link modifications, using the human-readable page title for context.

Upon successful translation of a file, the controller must extract the page's title using BeautifulSoup (falling back to the filename) and log it as '[System] TranslatedPage: {page_title} | {filepath}'.

The text logs are parsed and visualized by the DashboardGenerator (app/core/dashboard_generator.py) into '{CourseName} Translation Report.xlsx' saved in the Reports/ directory. The dashboard includes a 'Dashboard' tab showing the Course Name & Code, KPI metrics, skipped files list, and file type counts; a 'Bot Analysis' tab with per-bot statistics and a stacked chart; a 'Raw Logs' tab with all parsed log entries; a 'Translated Pages' tab listing deduplicated translated page titles (flagging any duplicate names with 'Duplicate Name (FIX EN Course)'); and a 'Link Actions' tab.

The 'Link Actions' tab consolidates Google Links (which get stripped of tracking parameters and flagged with 'FIX EN Course'), Skipped Links (logged as Info without warnings), and Commented Links (where users provided notes during link mapping).

api_assignments.ChatGPT: Use for OCR of images containing embedded text. (Note: Standalone image replacement agents are currently unimplemented).
api_assignments.Claude: Use for HTMLTranslationAgent, XMLTranslationAgent, QTITranslationAgent, and DocumentTranslationAgent (docx, pptx). Crucial for strict adherence to complex formatting constraints, preserving brackets, and ensuring zero tag modification. (Note: Document agents are currently unapproved/unimplemented).
api_assignments.Gemini: All current bots (controller, HTML, XML, text, image, auditor, scripturecheck, qa_audit) currently default to using gemini-1.5-flash for translation, multimodal image description, and processing.

api_resilience.rate_limits: All bots MUST implement an exponential backoff retry mechanism (via app/bots/api_utils.py call_gemini_with_retry) to gracefully handle 429 Rate Limit errors, internal server errors (500/503), 504 Gateway Timeouts, and deadline exceeded errors, given the concurrency of translations.
api_resilience.invalid_keys: All bots MUST validate their API keys on initialization (checking key presence via the client_ready flag) and the shared api_utils catches 400 Bad Request/InvalidArgument exceptions to prevent empty file overwrites or silent failures.

multi_agent_strategy.controller_bot: The primary bot (controller.py) acts as the controller. Its responsibility is to iterate through the directory structure and files in two phases. Phase 1: Sequential link pre-processing (delegated to LinkProcessor in app/core/link_processor.py), where it extracts URLs from href attributes, <url> tags (in XML), and applies a universal fallback regex. It automatically ignores standard namespaces (w3.org, purl.org, imsglobal.org), Canvas internal paths (instructure.com, canvas file links), Google user content images (googleusercontent.com), and BYU-I LTI links (byui-lti-to-url.azurewebsites.net). It checks against app/link_mapping.json, tracks session-skipped links to avoid double-prompting, extracts the human-readable page/quiz title to provide context, prompts the user via UI for unmapped links (and optional comments), and updates files with localized links. Phase 2: Concurrent file delegation (via ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=3) to specialized subagents for translation. It MUST NOT perform LLM translations itself.
multi_agent_strategy.specialized_bots: For each file or specific file type (e.g., HTML, XML), the controller bot MUST invoke a specialized subagent/bot to perform the actual parsing and translation.
multi_agent_strategy.scripturecheck_bot: A local pre-processing utility (scripturecheck_bot.py) that uses Regular Expressions to extract scripture references from the source text and fetches their official translations from the 'Glossary/scriptures/{lang}/' folder (where lang is 'por' for PTBR or 'spa' for SPA) to be injected into the translation prompt as constraints. TODO: Extend to support Bible references.
multi_agent_strategy.glossary_audit_bot: A local pre-processing utility (auditor_bot.py, class GlossaryAuditBot) that scans the source text for English glossary terms from Glossary/glossary.json and passes only the relevant glossary terms (filtered by target language) as constraints to the translation prompt.
multi_agent_strategy.qa_audit_bot: A specialized subagent (qa_audit_bot.py, class QAAuditBot) used by course_auditor.py. Has two capabilities: (1) audit_content() which compares the English (Canon) Canvas page against its translated counterpart, identifying Missing, Extra, Different Content, and Different Order discrepancies; (2) pair_unmatched_files() which uses AI to match unmatched English files to their translated counterparts when filenames have changed (e.g., W03 → S03 renaming scenarios).

agent_mapping.html: HTMLTranslationAgent (html_bot.py) - Responsible for parsing HTML DOM using BeautifulSoup to dynamically map and protect sensitive attributes (like src and href URLs) with UUID placeholders before translating textual content. It also delegates tags to ImageProcessorBot for alt text translation/generation.
agent_mapping.xml: XMLTranslationAgent (xml_bot.py) - Responsible for safely translating localized text strings inside XML tags using BeautifulSoup. Extracts only the inner text of specific nodes and translates them via a custom XML-like delimiter. It also delegates tags within inner HTML to ImageProcessorBot for alt text translation/generation.
agent_mapping.qti: QTITranslationAgent - Maps to XMLTranslationBot, sharing the same class as XML. Responsible for specialized Canvas QTI assessment files (quizzes), ensuring assessment structures remain valid.
agent_mapping.txt: TextTranslationAgent (txt_bot.py) - Responsible for plain text file translation.
agent_mapping.docx: DocumentTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED/PENDING APPROVAL] Responsible for extracting, translating, and repacking Microsoft Word documents.
agent_mapping.pptx: DocumentTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED/PENDING APPROVAL] Responsible for extracting, translating, and repacking Microsoft PowerPoint presentations.
agent_mapping.jpg: ImageTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED] For localized versions of images. Note: Alt text is handled inline by ImageProcessorBot.
agent_mapping.DS_Store: IGNORE - System files should be skipped by the controller.
agent_mapping.UNKNOWN: CRITICAL: Any unmapped file extension should trigger the unknown_architecture_protocol.

translation_guidelines: The target language for all translations will be either Portuguese (Brazil) or Spanish, as directed by the user.
Only translate textual content intended for students.
The setup notes page (files containing 'setup-notes') should be completely skipped and NOT translated.

For files related to the Teaching Notes and Student Outreach page (e.g., containing 'teaching-notes-and-student-outreach'), the controller must automatically apply a hardcoded glossary of Canvas navigation terms to ensure instructor-facing terminology matches expected standards. NOTE: The current hardcoded glossary is Portuguese-only and must be extended for Spanish when SPA translation of Teaching Notes pages is needed.

For files related to the Teaching Notes and Student Outreach page, the bots must empty the contents of the 'Release Notes' section (leaving only the translated 'Release Notes' header), as translated courses start with a fresh version history.
For XML question banks and quizzes, the word 'Question' in the title attribute of <item> nodes must be translated to the target language.
Preserve all HTML structure, Canvas-specific classes, div wrappers, and inline styles exactly as they are.

Preserve all XML tags, attributes, and file names. Do not translate metadata keys, IDs, or manifest identifiers (except for the 'title' attribute on <item> nodes where 'Question' is translated, and the <fieldentry> content for 'bank_title' labels).
Ensure translated HTML or XML does not break parsing rules.

Whenever the controller finds a churchofjesuschrist.org link, it must change the link parameter to the target language (e.g., lang=por for Portuguese or lang=spa for Spanish). If no lang parameter exists, one is appended.

The controller must programmatically replace the standalone word 'Missing' (or 'missing') in XML files (like rubrics) with 'Não Entregue' (for PTBR) or 'No Entregado' (for SPA) prior to passing the content to the XML bot, to ensure accurate rubric rendering.
The XML bot must explicitly skip translating the exact strings 'True' and 'False' inside <mattext> tags to prevent Canvas from demoting true_false_question types to Multiple Choice during import.
bot_instructions.unknown_architecture_protocol: If the controller encounters a file type that is not mapped to an active bot, it must gracefully skip the file and log a warning ('Skipping unsupported file architecture for extension...'). It should not halt execution.
bot_instructions.user_intervention_required: User intervention is not required for unknown file types; the controller will simply skip them and proceed with the rest of the translation batch.

agent_prompts.HTMLTranslationAgent_PTBR:
Role & Objective

You are an expert academic translator specializing in Portuguese. Your singular objective is to translate text within HTML tags into standard, grammatically correct Portuguese that is universally understood across all Portuguese-speaking regions (including Europe, Africa, and Brazil), appropriate for undergraduate students. In the rare event of an irreconcilable regional conflict, fall back to Brazilian Portuguese conventions.

Input Context

You will receive fragmented HTML chunks. The code will often be incomplete or have unmatched/open tags.

Strict Constraints

Localization & Transcreation: DO NOT translate word-by-word. Your goal is to LOCALIZE the content. Restructure sentences, use natural idiomatic phrasing, and adapt expressions so they read fluidly and professionally to a native speaker. Preserve the original intent, tone, and academic rigor, but prioritize natural flow over literal translation.

Output Format: You MUST wrap your entire final output inside an HTML markdown code block (```html at the beginning and ``` at the end). Never output raw HTML outside of these backticks.

Zero Interaction: Do NOT output any conversational filler, greetings, acknowledgments, or explanations. Only output the code block.

Zero Tag Modification: Do NOT translate, modify, add, or remove ANY HTML tags. Do NOT attempt to "fix" or auto-close open tags. Output the exact original tag structure. Translate ONLY inner text values.

Formatting Integrity: Maintain exact original indentation, line breaks, and spacing of the HTML structure.

Language & Gender Neutrality: Use grammatically correct, gender-neutral terminology naturally available in the language (e.g., prefer estudante over aluno(a) or pessoa over homem/mulher). Strict Restriction: You must completely avoid artificial gender-neutral word endings (such as substituting "o" or "a" with "e") and neologisms (such as todes).

STRICT WHITESPACE NORMALIZATION: You must NEVER output the invisible Alt+0160 character (non-breaking space / U+00A0), and you must NEVER output the HTML entity  . You must actively replace any non-breaking spaces or   entities from the original text with standard normal spaces (U+0020) in your final output.

Institutional Guidelines

Deity & Reverence: Capitalize all names, titles, and pronouns referring to Deity (e.g., Ele, Dele). However, lowercase pronouns referring to heavenly parents.  

Scriptural Formats: Do not italicize the titles of the standard works or their specific parts (e.g., Bíblia, O Livro de Mórmon).  

Church Nomenclature: Always use the full official name of the Church as defined in the glossary. Do not use terms like "Mormon Church", "LDS Church", or "Mormonism".  

Quotation Integrity: Maintain the exact formatting, spelling, and punctuation of quoted material. If an interpolation, translation of a term, or grammatical correction is necessary within a quote, you must enclose the added text in brackets [ ].  \n\nRelease Notes: When translating Teaching Notes or Student Outreach pages, empty out all content under the 'Release Notes' section (e.g. leaving only the translated <summary> or heading), as translated courses start with a fresh version history.

workflow: The UI prompts the user to select the English (Original) and Translated IMSCC files.
The system internally copies the selected .imscc files to the 'Courses to Audit/' directory.
The CourseAuditor extracts both Canvas packages into temporary 'temp_en' and 'temp_pt' folders inside 'Courses to Audit/'.
It reads the 'imsmanifest.xml' from both packages to securely map the unique Canvas 'identifier' for each file to its relative path.

It cross-references all translatable files (.html and .xml) globally across the entire course to determine matching pairs using a multi-step strategy: (1) Match by Manifest Resource ID, (2) Fallback to Relative Path matching, (3) AI-based pairing via QAAuditBot.pair_unmatched_files() for handling renamed files (e.g., W03 → S03), (4) Flag remaining unmatched EN files as 'Missing in Translated', and (5) Flag remaining unmatched PT files as 'Extra in Translated'.
The auditor iterates through every matched file pair.
For HTML pages, it performs a strict link audit to verify all external web URLs (http/https) match exactly between English and Translated pages, flagging any missing or extra links.

For files containing sufficient text (length > 10), it leverages gemini-3.5-flash via the QAAuditBot to perform an advanced LLM-based quality assurance check, categorizing discrepancies as Missing, Extra, Different Content, or Different Order.

The results are safely parsed and exported directly into a 3-tab Excel report ('Audit_Report_{CourseName}.xlsx') saved in the Reports/ directory: 'Page Audit Report' (file level match status with EN/PT page names), 'Content Audit Report' (text/layout/meaning discrepancies from LLM analysis), and 'Links Audit Reports' (URL discrepancies for HTML pages).

utility_scripts.reprocess_failed.py: A utility script that parses the translation_log.txt to find files that failed on the 3rd XML parse attempt, re-initializes the TranslationController, and reprocesses only those failed files. NOTE: This script currently has a broken call to controller.compress_to_imscc() which should be controller.workspace.compress_to_imscc(controller._log).
